**_claude re-provision — STAGED, blocked on one Drew-physical step (2026-11-07 ~22:35 CST)**

Re-verified on the laptop this pass: `~/.claude/.credentials.json` mtime 19:02:10 CST, accessToken len 0, refreshToken len 0, expiresAt 0, subscriptionType "max" retained; `claude auth status` → loggedIn false. Legacy proxy units (claude-code-proxy, commandcode-proxy) are inactive — not the live writer this time.

Restore staged per the 2026-11-06 route (stock Chromium on the laptop, never Helium, never the sandbox browser):
- `claude auth login` running in laptop tmux `claude-relogin`, alive and waiting at "Paste code here".
- Stock Chromium (CDP 19224, profile /tmp/chromium-auth) driven to the claude.ai re-auth login; account verified from the laptop's own `~/.claude.json` oauthAccount metadata: drewrypope@gmail.com, organizationType claude_max.
- Magic link requested from that Chromium at 22:23 CST; the email arrived ("Your secure link to Claude is here", 22:23:21 CST). The Chromium tab is parked on "To continue, click the link sent to drewrypope@gmail.com".

**The one Drew step** — the link must be opened in that laptop Chromium window, and no fleet route can fetch it: Helium's Gmail is sitting behind Google's "Verify it's you" re-sign-in (password = Drew's), and the Gmail connector returns the sign-in link only as a redacted credential reference that cannot be redeemed on the laptop surface. Either:
- **(A)** On the laptop, complete "Verify it's you" in Helium (a Gmail tab is already open on that prompt) — the fleet then extracts the link from Gmail exactly as on 2026-11-06 and finishes everything itself; or
- **(B)** Copy the "Sign in" link from the Anthropic email (sent 22:23) and paste it into the address bar of the stock Chromium window on the laptop (the one showing the "click the link" message).

Immediately after either: fleet clicks Authorize on the OAuth consent screen, pastes the callback code into the waiting CLI, verifies the credential by structure, restarts opencode.service + the OpenClaw gateway (sequenced after the in-flight config lanes' writes land — the speedswitch lane was actively writing opencode.jsonc at 22:30 CST), and verifies _claude successes plus sonnet-plan/haiku-plan samples before task 12765 is completed. Nothing has been restarted or edited by this lane yet.

Root cause + fix report (2026-11-08, credential-blanking lane).

## Writer inventory (verified on the laptop)
- The only first-party writer of `~/.claude/.credentials.json` in the deployed stack is the opencode fork's `writeCredential` / `buildCredentialsFileContents` (`packages/ai/src/providers/claude-code-auth.ts`). The fork's quota provider, OpenChamber's quota code, and the aggregator gatherer are all read-only for this file. The other writer is the real Claude CLI itself.
- Triage task 12765's finding is confirmed live today: the file on disk is still the 2026-11-07 19:02:10 write - access token length 0, refresh token length 0, expiresAt 0, subscriptionType "max" retained. Fix task 12770 had NOT landed a guard: the only sibling work is fork PR #2172 (temp-file cleanup in the same helper), which does not touch token emptiness.

## The defect, reproduced
The fork's write boundary performed no validation at all: the helper serializes whatever blob it is handed, merging over the prior file. Reproduction against current main (pre-fix): handing `writeCredential` the exact incident shape persists it verbatim - access length 0, refresh length 0, expiresAt 0, plan retained. The refresh path also persisted a present-but-empty `refresh_token` and an `expires_in` of 0 verbatim. The read side was hardened for this class in #1763/#1765; the write side never was.

## The 2026-11-07 19:02 write itself
At 19:02:10.236 the real CLI wrote its headless-failure marker (`~/.claude/cache/model-catalog/*.cc.headless-failed.json`); at 19:02:10.638 the credentials file was rewritten. The fork build running then (service started 2026-11-06 13:17, pre-#1818) had no refresh write-back at all and its sign-in path refuses an empty access token, so that specific write most plausibly came from the real Claude CLI serializing an empty in-memory credential after a failed refresh of an already-expired session. Surviving logs cannot prove the invoking process; either way, the fixable defects in our own setup are the two below.

## Fixes landed
1. developing-today-forks/opencode PR #2173 (merge c6766d8a): a hard invariant at the write boundary - new `ClaudeCodeCredentialWriteError` + `assertPersistableOAuthBlob`, enforced inside `buildCredentialsFileContents` so every caller of the serializer and of `writeCredential` is covered. Empty/whitespace access token, present-but-empty/whitespace refresh token, or a non-positive expiry is refused by name before any write; the existing file stays byte-identical. `refreshAndPersist` and the sign-in exchange also reject a present-but-empty `refresh_token` / present-but-invalid `expires_in` as a malformed success (tokens discarded, file unchanged). 10 new regression tests (empty refresh response fields, HTTP error, malformed JSON, happy-path rotation): `bun test test/provider/claude-code-auth.test.ts` 52 pass / 0 fail. Typecheck shows only the pre-existing `secret-service.ts` @napi-rs/keyring error, identical on main.
2. developing-today/code PR #7824 (merge 6b94b29d): the agent-backup snapshot set covered `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.claude.json` but NOT `~/.claude/.credentials.json` - which is why every blanking costs a full manual re-sign-in: no known-good copy existed anywhere to restore from. The file is now in the snapshot candidates and in the path unit's PathChanged triggers, so every rewrite (sign-in, CLI rotation, or a blanking) leaves a dated snapshot and the last good pair survives.

## Deploy state
Both PRs are merged but NOT yet deployed, deliberately: the Claude re-sign-in restore is still in flight (`claude auth status` still loggedIn false; the file is still the blanked one). Per sequencing, nothing restarts until the restore lands. After it does: the fork fix rides the next production opencode build/switch, the agent-backup change rides the next home switch, and acceptance is a forced refresh cycle + one more service restart proving the file still holds non-empty tokens and `opencode quota` returns a live Claude row.

## Named last-resort follow-on (proposed, not settled for)
If blanking recurs after these land - i.e. the closed-source CLI blanks it again - the next step is a file-watch/restore guard: a path unit that restores the last non-empty agent-backup snapshot whenever the file lands blank. It is a last resort and is named here rather than silently adopted.

**"Who invoked the CLI" — closed out (2026-11-08, Drew's order: "the real claude cli shouldn't be doing anything")**

**Attribution for the 2026-11-07 19:02 run — graded:**
- PROVEN: a real `claude` binary headless run executed at 19:02:10.210 CST (marker `{"failedAt":1794099730210,"failures":1}` in `~/.claude/cache/model-catalog/`); `.credentials.json` was rewritten blank 0.4s later (19:02:10.638). The run's footprint is confined to `~/.claude` — no other file on the box was touched in that window. No systemd unit/timer or cron started it (user journal for that minute shows only autocommit, queue-expire, external-comms, pm-git-sync).
- NOT PROVEN: the OpenClaw ACP wrapper was the invoker. It was the only *configured* automated path to the binary, and the gateway was running — but there is no claude ACP session record anywhere (gateway `acp_sessions` table and on-disk acpx records hold only opencode sessions), and the gateway writes no journal log for that window. A sandbox-side lane driving the laptop over SSH also cannot be ruled out from laptop-side evidence. The invoker remains unattributed; what is fixed is that the path can no longer be taken.

**Inventory of automated invokers (laptop, verified 2026-11-08):** exactly one — OpenClaw's acpx `claude` agent (gateway `acp.allowedAgents` + embedded acpx `agents.claude.command`, plus the standalone `~/.acpx/config.json` entry), all pointing at `~/.openclaw/acpx/claude-agent-acp-wrapper.mjs` → vendored `claude-agent-acp` adapter → the real CLI. Clean: all systemd user units/timers (none exec the binary), cron (none), shell profiles, `~/tools` scripts, fleet `bin/` scripts, OpenCode/OpenChamber (native provider only, never execs the binary).

**Disabled:**
1. The wrapper is now a fail-closed stub (exit 1, never spawns anything), live immediately and committed by the .openclaw autocommit (4b46f020). The vendored adapter is preserved beside it as `claude-agent-acp-wrapper.mjs.vendor-original` (code#6166 work intact).
2. PR #7832 (merged, bfcfd2c8cf): `home/openclaw/default.nix` drops `claude` from `acp.allowedAgents`, drops the acpx `agents.claude` override, and drops the `claude` entry from the generated `~/.acpx/config.json`. The laptop primary checkout is fast-forwarded to that merge, so the generated configs lose claude at the next NixOS switch. A dedicated switch was attempted but the fleet rebuild script requires an interactive sudo password no agent can supply; until any switch runs, the stub in (1) is the operative block — the only command either config can execute for `claude` is the stub.
3. Untouched per the sanctioned list: the CLI stays installed (`claude --version` = 2.1.306), and the waiting `claude-relogin` / `claude-login2` tmux `claude auth login` sessions were not disturbed (PIDs verified unchanged).

**Verification:** an ACP `initialize` sent to the configured claude command (exactly what acpx executes) exits 1 with the disabled message and spawns no child; an ACP bridge session attempt against the gateway likewise produced no `claude` process. Only the two sanctioned `claude auth login` processes exist on the box; the model-catalog dir still holds only the 2026-11-07 marker, and `.credentials.json` still carries its 2026-11-07 19:02:10 mtime — nothing has run the CLI since.

**Record correction — the 2026-11-10 _claude auth wave (minder escalation, comment 6776585228): the login was never dead.**

The escalation framed the _claude route head as auth-dead with a login "no longer renewable." Wire verification by the fix lane shows that framing was wrong:

- The server's credential row for claude-code is a pointer to `~/.claude/.credentials.json`. The server's own refresh path attempted renewal **22 seconds after** the access token expired (18:48:38Z, Nov 10) and got **HTTP 429 — a rate limit — from Anthropic's refresh endpoint on the first try**. The code mislabeled that 429 in its error text as "the CLI's login is no longer renewable" and classified it **Authentication**; every session request then retried the exchange, producing **1,176 Authentication failures in 26 minutes** (waves 11:40–12:55 CST).
- The login itself was healthy the whole time: the stored refresh token never stopped being valid (refresh expiry **2026-12-07**, unchanged), and the moment a fresh access token existed the door recovered to **76 successes / 0 Authentication failures** with no re-sign-in.
- So the failure was a **misclassified refresh 429 plus no wait/fallback in the server's renewal path** — not a dead login, and not a quota problem.

Fix (Drew's rule: self-renewal in-server, wait out the rate limit honoring `Retry-After`, renew early, no CLI involvement): fork [PR #2255](https://github.com/developing-today-forks/opencode/pull/2255) (the renewal wait-out fix pull request), merged `3497ea22c946` — 2-hour early renewal lead, 429 waits (Retry-After or capped backoff, 15-minute budget, single-flight), door held in a rate-limit hold while renewal is pending, budget exhaustion surfaces RateLimit never Authentication, "no longer renewable" wording removed. Pin via code [PR #8232](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8232) (the opencode pin bump pull request) merged `0ecd3f9052`. **Running build proven 2026-11-10 ~14:59 CST: 2.0.30+3497ea2** (pid 2570956, session API 200). Full verdict: [#6120 comment 6779176506](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6120#issuecomment-6779176506) (the renewal verdict comment); audit row updated on [#8102](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/8102) (the provider self-renewal audit issue).

## Credential-blanking fixes: deployed + acceptance-tested (2026-11-12)

**Guard (fork PR developing-today-forks/opencode#2173) is LIVE in production.** As of 2026-11-12 19:36:28Z, `opencode.service` runs `opencode-2.0.30+0f5561c-wrapped` (fork rev `0f5561c21cb8`, which contains the guard merge `c6766d8ad550`). Proof: the running process exe resolves to that build, and the guard symbol `ClaudeCodeCredentialWriteError` is present in it (2 occurrences) and absent (0) in the previously running `8ed9d6c` build. Deployed by repointing the service's existing binary-pin drop-in (`~/.config/systemd/user/opencode.service.d/zz-8653-binary-restore.conf`, the mechanism production has run under since the Nov 11 #8653 rollback) at the wrapped package built from the current flake inputs, then `daemon-reload` + restart.

**Why not a full nixos switch:** today's `origin/main` (`670be02612`) cannot build a switchable system — four stacked breakages, found in sequence:
1. Evaluation fails: `programs.openclaw` assertion rejects the `memory-wiki` plugin id (from `d42d6cb3c3`, Nov 12 00:06 CST). Fix already open as **PR #8949**.
2. `pkgs/id` lib fails to compile (`world_ws.rs` uses `pub(crate)` id-worlds internals after the crate split). Fix already open as **PR #8818**.
3. `pkgs/id` test `probe_attestation_sign` doesn't compile against the 6-arg `sign_claim`. Fix already open as **PR #8785**.
4. **No fix yet:** `id-core` test `frames::tests::byte_refusal_does_not_spend_a_frame_token_or_increment_counters` fails deterministically (verified in the nix sandbox AND standalone via cargo: `charge_frame` returns `RequestTooLarge`, the test expects `BudgetExhausted` for a 5-byte frame against `byte_burst: 4`). With `doCheck = true` this fails the `id` package build, so the toplevel cannot build. This one is for the id lane to settle (impl precedence vs test expectation).

A deploy tree with the three available fixes cherry-picked onto `670be02612` is left at `~/git/code-wt-7098-deploy` on the laptop. Once #8949 / #8818 / #8785 merge and the frames test is fixed, a plain switch converges everything, and the drop-in pin can be retired when the unit's own build reaches a guarded rev. (The `fleet` package also flaked once during these builds — one `fleet-proxy` lib test died with EINTR under load, then passed on retry.)

**Backup half (code PR #7824): already deployed and verified live.** The deployed `agent-backup.path` includes `PathChanged=%h/.claude/.credentials.json` and the deployed script lists the file in its snapshot candidates. Live proof today: when the token rotated at 18:57:05Z, the path unit fired automatically — snapshots `2026-11-12T18-57-05` / `T18-57-06` contain `.claude/.credentials.json` (558 bytes) and the `latest` symlink points at the rotation snapshot.

**Acceptance (the one owed since Nov 8):**
- Baseline 18:25Z: tokens non-empty (access 108 chars, refresh 108 chars), expiry 18:50:57Z, `claude auth status` loggedIn true.
- The token expired at 18:50:57Z; a refresh cycle ran at **18:57:05Z** and persisted a fresh pair — lengths still 108/108, new expiry 2026-11-13T02:57:05Z, **no blanking**. (Writer attribution for that rotation isn't provable from logs; it succeeded, which is the non-destructive case either way. As of the 19:36Z restart, every credential writer path is a guarded build: the server at `0f5561c`, and the gatherer's quota subcommand was already running a guarded system build.)
- After the restart onto the guarded build: tokens still 108/108, `claude auth status` still loggedIn true, and the gatherer's `_claude` row stayed fresh — measured 2026-11-12T19:39:05Z, state ok, 5h 96%, 7d 47%, Fable:7d 21%, plan max.

If blanking ever recurs with all writers guarded, the writer is outside the guard (e.g. the real CLI — its automated ACP invoker remains disabled/stubbed since Nov 8) and the snapshot-restore guard proposed earlier on this issue is the next step.

**Deploy + acceptance of the blanking fixes — COMPLETE (2026-11-12, post-restore)**
